Matching the seizure syndrome

A 7-year-old girl has frequent brief staring episodes with immediate recovery and no history of convulsive seizures. Hyperventilation provokes an episode, and EEG shows generalized 3-Hz spike-and-wave activity. Which medication specifically targets this seizure syndrome?

  1. Carbamazepine
  2. Gabapentin
  3. Phenylephrine
  4. Ethosuximide
  5. Phenytoin
Answer and explanation

Ethosuximide

The presentation is typical absence epilepsy, for which ethosuximide is an established treatment.

Option explanations

Ethosuximide: The presentation is typical absence epilepsy, for which ethosuximide is an established treatment.

Phenytoin: Phenytoin is not an appropriate treatment for typical absence seizures.

Carbamazepine: Carbamazepine may aggravate absence seizures.

Gabapentin: Gabapentin is not a standard treatment for this generalized absence syndrome.

Phenylephrine: This adrenergic agonist is not an antiseizure treatment.
